#baking #pastry

All-butter pie crust, the one that finally works, written down 3 May 2025. 300 g plain flour, 200 g Lurpak unsalted (cubed, frozen 15 min), 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp caster sugar, 1 tsp cider vinegar stirred into 90 ml iced water and you'll use 70 to 80 ml of it. That's 3:2:1 flour, fat, water, near enough. Rub in until the biggest butter bits are pea-sized and you can still see streaks, bring together, don't knead. Two discs, cling film, fridge 2 hours minimum, overnight better. Roll to 3 mm, line a 23 cm loose-base tin, leave 1 cm overhang, freeze 20 min. Blind bake at 200°C with 600 g of the old dried chickpeas I use as baking beans, 20 min, beans out, brush the base with egg white, 8 more min until matte and golden. Trim the overhang after, not before, it shrinks. Base stays crisp even under the wet Bramley apple filling (1.2 kg apples, 90 g sugar, 1 tbsp cornflour). Oven has to read true, see [[Oven thermometer calibration]], or add 10 min. Made 14 of these for the [[Bake sale 2025 notes]], cost £2.90 each, sold at £12.
